messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in us-west-2 (streaming) · SLOs breached for 3 routes · increased tail stalls. Automated severity: Sev2. Metrics: p95 x1.6, p99 x3.1, error-rate +0.8%. See: https://telemetry.internal/r/3472109876
Samira: I'm on it. grabbing graphs and recent deploys. @Jonah can you pull cache hit-rate and prefetch metrics for the streaming cluster?
Jonah: pulling now. preliminary: overall prefix-cache hit rate dropped from ~91% to ~7% starting at 3472104500 (approx 70m ago). Prefetch queue depth spiked. Paging ops to disk increased by ~4x.
Meera: that window aligns with the prefix-salting rollout we promoted at 3472104200 (canary -> 50%). I'm worried the new salt variant changed key namespace.
Samira: ok hypothesis: salt change produced cache key mismatch -> massive cold miss storm -> paging/prefetch backlog -> streaming stalls -> p99 spikes.
Jonah: supporting data: kvstore metrics show prefix_namespace:v2 counts higher than v1, but cache tier only populated for v1 keys. Also saw evictions TTL churn. Query sample:
```
# sample head of miss log
[3472104601] route=streaming-append key=prefix:v2:abc123 status=MISS
[3472104602] route=streaming-append key=prefix:v2:abc124 status=MISS
[3472104603] route=streaming-append key=prefix:v2:abc125 status=MISS
# hitrate summary
old_namespace_hits=92.3% new_namespace_hits=6.8% prefetch_queue=12k
```
Samira: nice. We need an immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact and buy time for rollback and fix. Propose: 1) Abort the salting rollout -> toggle flag to v1 2) Increase prefetch concurrency and TTL to warm cache faster 3) Route high-latency streaming requests to fallback model variant (shorter context) while cache warms 4) Notify affected customers + handoff to night oncall after mitigation. Thoughts? @Ops Deploy Bot runbook?
Ops Deploy Bot: Plan accepted. Recommended order: rollback rollout flag (fastest), then enable prefetch bump, then route adjustments. I can run rollout rollback if given thumbs.
Samira: Jonah/Meera please prepare the rollback command and prefetch config. I'll gate and run. Liam (CSM) please prepare a short note for affected customers if we see sustained p99 > 2x after rollback.
Jonah: rollback command (dry-run shown):
```
# rollback prefix-salting rollout to v1
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.internal/api/rollouts/namespace-salt -d '{"target": "v1", "force": true}'
# verify
curl https://controlplane.internal/api/rollouts/namespace-salt/status
```
Jonah: prefetch bump patch (hot):
```
# patch prefetch config
kubectl -n streaming patch cm prefetch-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"concurrency":"128","ttl_sec":"7200","aggressive_prefetch":"true"}}'
# restart prefetch workers gradually
kubectl -n streaming rollout restart sts/prefetch-worker -l batch=low-pri
```
Meera: also suggest increasing cache memory reservation on streaming cache nodes to avoid immediate evictions while warmup happens. Patch sent to infra.
Samira: executing rollback now. Will post progress.
Samira: (08:51) issuing rollback...
```
> curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/rollouts/namespace-salt -d '{"target":"v1","force":true}' -H 'Authorization: ***'
Response: accepted (202) rollout change started. change_id=chg-98321
```
Jonah: seeing initial change: traffic portion reduced for v2 canaries to 0% in 2m. Monitoring hit-rate...
Jonah: (09:03) hit-rate climbing: v1 hit-rate -> 43% ; prefetch queue dropping. p99 down from 3.1x to 1.9x. Good direction.
Meera: prefetch concurrency increase applied. TTL bumped. Prefetch logs show aggressive warmups hitting cache.
Samira: patch infra memory reservation applied. Evictions rate falling.
Samira: routing fallback enabled for three most impacted routes (streaming-append, chat-stream, long-context-run). Routing rule: if p99 > 1.8x OR cache_hit < 30% route -> model-small-fallback.
Ops Deploy Bot: routing update accepted.
Liam (CSM): drafting customer note. Earliest affected customers: cust-42, cust-81 (both using streaming). I'll coordinate with support to send targeted updates.
Samira: status update: p95 ~ baseline, p99 ~ 1.4x baseline, error-rate back to +0.2%. Outage window narrowed. Keep monitoring for 60m. If metrics plateau >1.6x escalate to Sev1.
Jonah: one anomalous datapoint: a small edge cluster (us-west-2-b) still shows low hit-rate. Investigating bucketed keys: looks like a truncated salt value was applied at that specific edge due to old config version on node agents. Rolling config sync to those nodes.
Meera: found a bug in the rollout script: it didn't update the namespace header in the gateway agent for nodes that had not rotated. Patch ready: gateway-agent: fix namespace header handling. Will deploy canary.
Samira: okay. Primary mitigation achieved (rollback + prefetch). Next: postmortem actions and follow-ups. I'll capture now and handoff to next oncall (Nick) at 10:30. Items: 1) Postmortem: root cause: rollout of prefix-salting variant v2 that changed namespace format; rollout system didn't ensure gateway-agent header sync -> partial key mismatch. 2) Recovery timeline + impact numbers (p95/p99 deltas, customer-impacted list). 3) Fixes: a) stronger rollout gating for namespace changes b) config-version check in gateway agent c) automated cache-warmup for major namespace changes d) QA test for salting compatibility.
Nick (oncall): I'm taking post-mitigation watch. Please handoff the remaining follow-ups and customer comms.
Samira: handing off. Current state: rollback completed, cache hit-rate trending to normal, routing fallback active but will be removed after stable 120m. Please keep alerts to only paged-on regressions.
Nick (oncall): acknowledged. I'll monitor dashboards and pick up the postmortem doc.
incidents-bot: NOTE: incident toggled to "under observation". If p99 > 1.6x for 15m, auto-escalate.
Samira: TL;DR: prefix-salt rollout caused namespace mismatch -> cold-miss storm -> paging & prefetch backlog -> streaming tail latency spikes. Mitigation: rolled back rollout, bumped prefetch/TTL, increased cache reservation, routing fallback, targeted customer notifications, handoff to oncall Nick. Postmortem owners: Meera/Jonah/Samira.
Liam (CSM): rough customer note: "We've seen transient streaming latency spikes due to a cache key namespace change during a configuration rollout. We rolled back the change and applied mitigations; performance is returning to normal. We'll follow up with a full postmortem and timeline." Would like review from eng before sending.
Meera: ack. I'll review then we can send.
Samira: thanks team. closing live thread but keeping it pinned to oncall.
